sample.justification: The arrival of Bingley establishes the marriage-driven premise briskly, but the scene mainly introduces the Bennet household and its status quo.
The conversation about judgment and marriage plants thematic questions, but it advances the plot only slightly.
Jane’s illness brings Elizabeth to Netherfield and deepens the central relationships while much of the scene remains introductory.

sample.summary: Momentum depends on a tightly timed chain: marriage and inheritance pressure is established early, attraction and misjudgment build before separation, and withheld information converts into escalating family danger. The long pauses between major turns remain effective because each one sustains a live uncertainty or raises the cost of the next choice.

firstFinding.headline: The marriage plot has material pressure from the outset.
bullets: The entail and the limited maternal fortune make marriage a practical security issue, not merely a romantic goal.
This pressure gives Mrs. Bennet’s matchmaking urgency and later makes the cost of Elizabeth’s refusal of Collins legible.
firstFinding.subject: Inheritance and marriage stakes
firstFinding.evidenceQuote: Mr. Bennet’s property consisted almost entirely in an estate of two thousand a year, which, unfortunately for his daughters, was entailed, in default of heirs male, on a distant relation; and their mother’s fortune, though ample for her situation in life, could but ill supply the deficiency of his.
